synopsis: Bosch's tram collision assistance combines camera and radar to detect vehicles, pedestrians and cyclists, warn the driver and brake automatically; Bosch says the technology was adapted from automotive systems [f1417, f15774, f1419, f15776]. Approval for public transport was reported by 2016, but the development duration, physical-versus-virtual validation split and approving body's evidence package are not publicly established in the corpus [f1420, f15777, f1421, f1422, f15778, f1423]. Bosch presents radar as improving detection in fog, rain and at night, but this remains a vendor claim rather than independent validation evidence [f1418, f15775, f1746, f1749]. The tram system is therefore an industry signal supporting sensor diversity, not proof of its effectiveness or that radar alone resolves adverse-environment validation [f1748, f1749].
